about: What a person, a place or an object is known for: a few clauses, each with the verses that say it, in English, Ukrainian, German and Spanish, written by a language model and read twice more. Nothing here is shown on the site until it is approved: an entry answered 'approved' is loaded by the next load of the known-for step, one answered 'rejected' is not. 'declined' lists the records the first reading gave no line, with its reason.
source: Essenthos, what a record is known for, written from its verses in the King James Version with the verses each clause rests on by claude-sonnet-5-5 on 2026-10-25, read again clause by clause against those verses and rendered into Ukrainian, German and Spanish by a second, separate reading, the renderings read by a third; on the project owner's instruction, each record shown once he has approved it

clauses.spa: se puso entre los muertos y los vivos con incienso y detuvo la mortandad
clauses.renderingsChanged: В українському рядку «поразка» (у сучасній мові «поразка» означає програш) замінено на «мор» — це відповідає англійському «plague».

clauses.english: died on Mount Hor, and his garments were put on Eleazar his son
clauses.ukr: помер на Гор-горі, а його шати були надягнені на його сина Елеазара
clauses.deu: starb auf dem Berg Hor, und seine Kleider wurden seinem Sohn Eleasar angezogen
clauses.spa: murió en el monte de Hor, y sus vestidos fueron puestos a Eleazar su hijo

first.reason: Aaron's story is told at length, so a few chief deeds can be drawn from the verses given: speaking with Moses to Pharaoh, making the golden calf, being consecrated priest, and dying on Mount Hor.
doubts: The clause on the calf cites EXO 32:4, which is not marked as naming Aaron; it is given as context beside EXO 32:1-5.
Marked verses naming only Aaron's sons or 'house of Aaron' (the priestly line) were left out as concerning others.
The Luke 1:5 verse 'daughters of Aaron' refers to descent, not to Aaron's deeds, so it was left out.

second.why: The cited verses say he went in to Pharaoh and cast down his rod; the speaking is in 7:7, not cited.

first.english: spoke to Pharaoh with Moses and cast down his rod, which became a serpent

second.why: The verses show Moses washing, clothing and anointing Aaron; his sons were only washed, and 'to serve as priest' is not stated.

first.english: was anointed and consecrated with his sons to serve as priest

second.why: 'At Sinai' is not in the verses; the calf was made from the people's golden earrings, and he built an altar before it.

first.english: made the golden calf for the people at Sinai

clauses.english: prayed and vowed to give a son to the LORD, and Eli thought she was drunken
clauses.ukr: молилася до Господа й склала обітницю віддати сина Господеві, а Ілій вважав її п'яною

clauses.spa: oró al SEÑOR e hizo voto de dar un hijo al SEÑOR, y Eli la tuvo por borracha

clauses.english: bore Samuel and brought him to the house of the LORD in Shiloh when he was weaned
clauses.ukr: породила Самуїла і привела його до дому Господнього в Шіло, коли він був відлучений
clauses.deu: gebar Samuel und brachte ihn in das Haus des HERRN zu Silo, als er entwöhnt war
clauses.spa: parió a Samuel y lo trajo a la casa del SEÑOR en Silo, cuando fue destetado

clauses.english: was visited by the LORD and bore three more sons and two daughters
clauses.ukr: була відвідана Господом і породила ще трьох синів та дві дочки
clauses.deu: wurde vom HERRN heimgesucht und gebar noch drei Söhne und zwei Töchter
clauses.spa: fue visitada por el SEÑOR y parió otros tres hijos y dos hijas

first.reason: The verses tell of Hannah's prayer and vow for a son and of her bringing Samuel to the LORD, which go beyond the summary.
doubts: Clause 1 joins the prayer with Eli's mistake; the second part may be trimmed as a minor detail.
The 'Hannah prayed' song of 1SA 2:1 was left out as praise rather than an event.

clauses.english: told Saul he had seen David come to Ahimelech at Nob
clauses.ukr: сказав Саулові, що бачив Давида, який приходив до Нова, до Ахімелеха
clauses.deu: sagte Saul, er habe David gesehen, wie er nach Nobe zu Ahimelech kam
clauses.spa: dijo a Saúl que había visto a David venir a Nob, a Ahimelech
clauses.renderingsChanged: Added the missing addressee Saul in all three languages.

clauses.english: slew eighty-five priests at Saul's command
clauses.ukr: вбив вісімдесят п'ять священиків за наказом Саула
clauses.deu: erschlug auf Befehl Sauls fünfundachtzig Priester
clauses.spa: mató a ochenta y cinco sacerdotes por orden de Saúl

first.reason: The verses tell two chief deeds of Doeg beyond the summary: his report to Saul and his slaying of the priests at Nob.
doubts: PSA 52:1 repeats the telling of Saul in a psalm title, so it was not cited separately.

second.why: The verses give Doeg's report that he saw David come to Nob to Ahimelech; verse 10 describes Ahimelech's deeds, so it should not be cited, and the report does not say David 'came to' him 'at Nob' in those words only.

first.english: told Saul he had seen David come to Ahimelech at Nob

readings.note: The line omits that Doeg also struck Nob, the city of the priests, with the sword (1SA 22:19), though it is not shown that he did it himself.

clauses.english: took Sisera into her tent when he fled, and gave him milk and covered him
clauses.ukr: прийняла Сісеру до свого намету, коли він утікав, напоїла його молоком і накрила його
clauses.deu: nahm Sisera in ihre Hütte auf, als er floh, gab ihm Milch zu trinken und deckte ihn zu
clauses.spa: recibió a Sísara en su tienda cuando huía, le dio de beber leche y lo cubrió

clauses.english: killed Sisera in his sleep by driving a tent nail into his temples
clauses.ukr: вбила Сісеру уві сні, забивши йому в скроню наметовий кілок
clauses.deu: tötete Sisera im Schlaf, indem sie ihm einen Zeltnagel durch die Schläfe schlug
clauses.spa: mató a Sísara mientras dormía, metiéndole una estaca de la tienda por las sienes
clauses.renderingsChanged: Ukrainian: «убила» changed to «вбила», the awkward «в його сні» to «уві сні», and the old accusative «кілка» to «кілок».

first.reason: The verses tell of Jael sheltering Sisera and then killing him with a tent nail, which is the story she is known for.
doubts: JDG 5:6 names Jael only to date a time of unsafe highways, so it was left out.
JDG 5:24 is a blessing pronounced on her, not an event, so it was left out.
The killing is told only once as an event, though the summary names Sisera's killer; JDG 4:22 and 5:26 repeat it.

clauses.english: slew six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and delivered Israel
clauses.ukr: побив шістсот филистимлян києм на худобу і урятував Ізраїля
clauses.deu: schlug sechshundert Philister mit einem Ochsenstecken und erlöste Israel
clauses.spa: hirió a seiscientos hombres de los filisteos con una aguijada de bueyes y salvó a Israel
clauses.renderingsChanged: Spanish: «Filisteos» is lower-cased to «filisteos» as modern usage requires.

first.reason: JDG 3:31 states Shamgar's deed and his deliverance of Israel; JDG 5:6 only dates a time of unsafe roads and adds no deed.
doubts: JDG 5:6 only names the days of Shamgar as a time when highways were unoccupied; it states no deed of his, so it is left out.

clauses.english: was taken by the children of Judah, smitten with the sword and set on fire
clauses.ukr: був здобутий Юдиними синами, побитий вістрям меча і підпалений
clauses.deu: wurde von den Kindern Juda eingenommen, mit der Schärfe des Schwerts geschlagen und angezündet
clauses.spa: fue tomada por los hijos de Judá, metida a cuchillo y puesta a fuego

clauses.english: was taken by David from the Jebusites and became the city of David
clauses.ukr: був узятий Давидом в євусеян і став Давидовим Містом
clauses.deu: wurde von David den Jebusitern abgenommen und wurde zu Davids Stadt
clauses.spa: fue tomada por David a los jebuseos y llegó a ser la Ciudad de David

clauses.english: was besieged by Nebuchadnezzar; its temple and houses were burned and its walls broken down
clauses.ukr: був обложений Навуходоносором; дім Господній і доми в ньому були спалені, а мури розбиті
clauses.deu: wurde von Nebukadnezar belagert; das Haus des HERRN und die Häuser wurden verbrannt und die Mauer zerbrochen
clauses.spa: fue cercada por Nabucodonosor; la casa del SEÑOR y las casas fueron quemadas y los muros derribados

first.reason: Jerusalem is a great city, and a few defining events of its story are plainly stated in the verses: its capture by Judah, David's taking of it, and its burning by the Chaldeans.
doubts: Marked verses naming Salem (GEN 14:18, HEB 7:1-2) concern Melchizedek's Salem; the verses here do not identify it with Jerusalem, so they were left out.
Jebus/Jebusite verses (JOS 15:63, JDG 1:21, JDG 19:10) were left out because the clauses chosen rest on stronger events.

second.why: The verses say the temple and houses were burned, but the walls were only broken down, not burned.

first.english: was besieged by Nebuchadnezzar, and its temple, houses and walls were burned and broken down

readings.note: The line does not say that Jerusalem was the city of the temple, or the place of later events such as the crucifixion of Jesus.

clauses.english: lost all its firstborn when the LORD smote them at midnight
clauses.ukr: втратив усіх перворідних, коли Господь вдарив їх опівночі
clauses.deu: verlor alle seine Erstgeburt, als der HERR sie um Mitternacht schlug
clauses.spa: perdió a todos sus primogénitos cuando el SEÑOR los hirió a la medianoche

clauses.english: saw its pursuing army overthrown by the LORD in the midst of the sea
clauses.ukr: побачив, як Господь кинув його військо, що гналося, у середину моря
clauses.deu: sah, wie der HERR sein verfolgendes Heer mitten ins Meer stürzte
clauses.spa: vio al SEÑOR derribar a su ejército perseguidor en medio del mar
clauses.renderingsChanged: Spanish: replaced the old-fashioned «la mar» with modern «el mar».

first.reason: Egypt is a whole land, so only the two events that fell on it alone are kept: the death of its firstborn and the drowning of its army.
doubts: Egypt appears in a very large number of verses, many only as a place of travel, a trading partner or a figure of speech; most were left out as not specific to the land.
Verses about Joseph's rule, the bondage of Israel, the plagues and the later prophecies against Egypt were deliberately omitted to keep the line to two events.

clauses.english: was where Jacob set up a stone pillar and named the place Bethel
clauses.ukr: був місцем, де Яків поставив камінь як пам'ятник і назвав те місце Бет-Елом
clauses.deu: war der Ort, an dem Jakob einen Stein als Mal aufrichtete und die Stätte Beth-El nannte
clauses.spa: fue donde Jacob alzó una piedra como monumento y llamó a aquel lugar Beth-el

clauses.english: was where Jeroboam set up one of two golden calves
clauses.ukr: був місцем, де Єровоам поставив одного з двох золотих тельців
clauses.deu: war der Ort, an dem Jerobeam eines von zwei goldenen Kälbern aufstellte
clauses.spa: fue donde Jeroboam puso uno de dos becerros de oro

clauses.english: was where Josiah broke down the altar and the high place and burned the high place
clauses.ukr: був місцем, де Йосія розбив жертовник і узвишшя та спалив узвишшя
clauses.deu: war der Ort, an dem Josia den Altar und die Höhe abbrach und die Höhe verbrannte
clauses.spa: fue donde Josías destruyó el altar y el alto, y quemó el alto

first.reason: Bethel is the scene of Jacob's naming of the place, Jeroboam's golden calf and Josiah's destruction of the altar, so a line of three events is warranted.
doubts: GEN 28:19 does not itself say what Jacob saw; the dream is only implied by the context verses given.
1KI 13:1 and 1KI 13:4 (the man of God against the altar) were left out as a separate event and for the limit on clauses.
1KI 16:34 (Hiel the Bethelite) names a man from Bethel, not the place itself, so it was not used.
JDG 1:22-25 (the house of Joseph taking the city) and 2CH 13:19 (Abijah taking the city) were left out for brevity.

second.why: Jeroboam is named only in verse 26, and there were two calves, one set in Bethel.

first.english: had a golden calf set up in it by Jeroboam

second.why: Josiah is named in verse 16, and only the high place was burned, not the altar.

first.english: had its altar and high place broken down and burned by Josiah

clauses.english: had its goods taken by Chedorlaomer and his allies, who also carried off Lot
clauses.ukr: був позбавлений маєтку Кедор-Лаомером та його союзниками, які забрали також Лота
clauses.deu: wurde von Kedor-Laomor und seinen Verbündeten, die auch Lot mitnahmen, seiner Habe beraubt
clauses.spa: fue despojada de sus riquezas por Chêdorlaomer y sus aliados, que se llevaron también a Lot
clauses.renderingsChanged: Ukrainian and German: the name now follows Ohienko (Кедор-Лаомер) and Luther (Kedor-Laomor). German: the relative clause is moved so «die» clearly refers to the allies.

clauses.english: was where its men surrounded Lot's house, demanding the two angels who had come to him
clauses.ukr: був місцем, де люди міста оточили дім Лота, вимагаючи видати двох ангелів, що прийшли до нього
clauses.deu: war der Ort, an dem die Männer der Stadt Lots Haus umringten und die zwei Engel forderten, die zu ihm gekommen waren
clauses.spa: fue el lugar donde los hombres de la ciudad cercaron la casa de Lot y exigieron que les entregaran a los dos ángeles que habían llegado a él
clauses.renderingsChanged: Spanish: «exigieron a los dos ángeles» made the angels the ones being asked, so it now says the men demanded that the angels be handed over.

clauses.english: was overthrown when the LORD rained brimstone and fire on it out of heaven
clauses.ukr: був зруйнований, коли Господь послав на нього з неба дощ із сірки й вогню
clauses.deu: wurde zerstört, als der HERR Schwefel und Feuer vom Himmel darauf regnen ließ
clauses.spa: fue destruida cuando el SEÑOR hizo llover sobre ella azufre y fuego desde el cielo
clauses.renderingsChanged: German: «auf es» replaced by the more natural «darauf».

first.reason: Sodom is a place where the story's events happened: its wickedness, its capture by the kings, and its destruction by fire from the LORD.
doubts: Left out the later verses that use Sodom as a comparison or warning (prophets, Gospels, epistles), since a comparison is not an event.
GEN 19:6-21 were not given, so the angels' dealings with Lot are not described.
EZK 16:49 and GEN 13:13 give Sodom's wickedness, but only as a character judgment, so no separate clause was written for it.
REV 11:8 calls another city 'Sodom' figuratively, so it was left out.

second.why: The verses say the kings took Sodom's goods and Lot, not that the city itself was taken; the actors are named in verse 9.

first.english: was taken and plundered by Chedorlaomer and his allies, who carried off Lot

second.why: The men demanded the guests be brought out; 'to get at' goes beyond this, and verse 3 is needed for Lot's house.

first.english: was where the men of the city surrounded Lot's house to get at the two angels who had come to him

clauses.english: routed about three thousand men of Israel and killed about thirty-six of them
clauses.ukr: змусив утікати близько трьох тисяч ізраїльтян і побив близько тридцяти шістьох із них
clauses.deu: schlug etwa dreitausend Mann Israels in die Flucht und erschlug etwa sechsunddreißig von ihnen
clauses.spa: puso en fuga a unos tres mil hombres de Israel y mató a unos treinta y seis de ellos
clauses.renderingsChanged: Ukrainian: replaced the non-standard «обернув навтікача» with «змусив утікати». Spanish: «hirió» changed to «mató» to match «killed», and «e» changed to «y».

clauses.english: was taken by an ambush and burnt by Joshua into a heap for ever
clauses.ukr: був здобутий засідкою і спалений Ісусом, обернений на вічну руїну
clauses.deu: wurde vom Hinterhalt eingenommen und von Josua niedergebrannt, zu einem ewigen Haufen gemacht
clauses.spa: fue tomado por la emboscada y quemado por Josué, reducido a un montón perpetuo
clauses.renderingsChanged: Ukrainian: removed «а потім», which is not in the English.

first.reason: Ai is the place where Israel was first defeated and then took the city by ambush and burned it.
doubts: Genesis verses spell the name Hai and only place Abram's tent beside it, so they were left out.
The Ezra and Nehemiah verses only list the men of Bethel and Ai, so they were left out.

second.why: The verses do not say it was Israel's first attack, and they give about three thousand men fleeing before Ai, not a 'rout' of the whole attack.

first.english: routed Israel's first attack, killing about thirty-six men

readings.note: The line omits that Israel's defeat at Ai was due to Achan's sin, and that Joshua hanged the king of Ai.

clauses.english: was made by Bezaleel of shittim wood overlaid with gold
clauses.ukr: був зроблений Бецал'їлом з акаційного дерева й обкладений золотом
clauses.deu: wurde von Bezaleel aus Akazienholz gemacht und mit Gold überzogen
clauses.spa: fue hecha por Bezaleel de madera de Sittim y cubierta de oro

clauses.english: was carried before Israel, and the waters of Jordan were cut off before it
clauses.ukr: був несений перед Ізраїлем, і йорданська вода була відділена перед ним
clauses.deu: wurde vor Israel her getragen, und das Wasser des Jordans riss vor ihr ab
clauses.spa: fue llevada delante de Israel, y las aguas del Jordán fueron partidas delante de ella

clauses.english: was taken by the Philistines in battle, and Dagon fell before it at Ashdod
clauses.ukr: був узятий филистимлянами в бою, а Даґон упав ницьма перед ним в Ашдоді
clauses.deu: wurde von den Philistern im Kampf genommen, und Dagon fiel in Asdod vor ihr auf sein Antlitz
clauses.spa: fue tomada por los Filisteos en la batalla, y Dagón cayó postrado delante de ella en Asdod

clauses.english: was brought up by David to the city of David, and Uzzah died for touching it
clauses.ukr: був винесений Давидом до Давидового Міста, а Узза помер за те, що доторкнувся до нього
clauses.deu: wurde von David in die Stadt Davids heraufgeholt, und Usa starb, weil er sie berührte
clauses.spa: fue traída por David a la ciudad de David, y Uzza murió por haberla tocado

clauses.english: was brought by the priests into the most holy place of the temple
clauses.ukr: був внесений священиками до Святого Святих храму
clauses.deu: wurde von den Priestern in das Allerheiligste des Tempels gebracht
clauses.spa: fue metida por los sacerdotes en el lugar santísimo del templo

first.reason: The verses tell the ark's story through its making, its crossing of Jordan, its capture by the Philistines, and its bringing to Jerusalem and the temple.
doubts: Several marked verses (such as 1SA 14:18 and 2SA 15:24-29) were not used because they are minor episodes beyond the chief events chosen.
1SA 6:19 is not used; the count of those smitten is uncertain and it is a lesser detail than the chief events.

second.why: The verses say the city of David, not Jerusalem, and do not say Uzzah died on the way.

first.english: was brought up to Jerusalem by David, and Uzzah died for touching it on the way

second.why: The verse says the priests brought the ark in, not Solomon.

first.english: was brought by Solomon into the most holy place of the temple

clauses.english: was made by Aaron from the people's golden earrings and worshipped with sacrifices as the gods who brought Israel out of Egypt
clauses.ukr: було зроблене Аароном із золотих сережок народу та вшановане поклонінням і жертвами як боги, що вивели Ізраїля з єгипетського краю
clauses.deu: wurde von Aaron aus den goldenen Ohrringen des Volkes gemacht und angebetet und mit Opfern verehrt als die Götter, die Israel aus Ägyptenland geführt haben
clauses.spa: fue hecho por Aarón con los pendientes de oro del pueblo y fue adorado con sacrificios como los dioses que sacaron a Israel de la tierra de Egipto
clauses.renderingsChanged: Ukrainian: «йому поклонялися» turned the clause round, now passive. German: modern «Ohrringen». Spanish: modern «pendientes», passive «fue adorado con sacrificios» instead of impersonal «se le sacrificó».

clauses.english: was burnt, ground to powder and scattered on the water by Moses, who made Israel drink of it
clauses.ukr: було спалене, змелене на порох і розсипане на воді Мойсеєм, який напоїв цим синів Ізраїлевих
clauses.deu: wurde verbrannt, zu Pulver zermalmt und aufs Wasser gestreut von Mose, der es den Kindern Israel zu trinken gab
clauses.spa: fue quemado, molido hasta reducirlo a polvo y esparcido sobre las aguas por Moisés, que lo dio a beber a los hijos de Israel
clauses.renderingsChanged: Removed «у вогні», «mit Feuer» and «en el fuego», which the English does not have. Ukrainian: «змолоте» corrected to «змелене». German: «und er gab» turned the clause round, now a relative clause on Mose.

first.reason: The verses tell what was done with the calf: it was made from the people's gold and worshipped, then Moses destroyed it.
doubts: EXO 32:35 says the LORD plagued the people because of the calf; left out as a deed of the people's punishment, not of the calf itself.
The clause about the making joins making and worship as one event in the story, citing EXO 32:2-4 and 32:8.

clauses.english: was made by Moses and set on a pole, so that those bitten by serpents who looked on it lived
clauses.ukr: був зроблений Мойсеєм і виставлений на жердині, щоб покусані зміями, які дивилися на нього, жили
clauses.deu: wurde von Mose gemacht und auf einer Stange aufgerichtet, damit die von Schlangen Gebissenen, die sie ansahen, lebten
clauses.spa: fue hecha por Moisés y puesta sobre un asta, para que los mordidos por serpientes que la miraban vivieran
clauses.renderingsChanged: Spanish: «bandera» (banner) replaced by «un asta», since the English says pole.

clauses.english: was broken in pieces by Hezekiah, because Israel had burned incense to it
clauses.ukr: був розбитий Єзекією, бо Ізраїль кадив йому
clauses.deu: wurde von Hiskia in Stücke zerschlagen, weil Israel ihr Weihrauch dargebracht hatte
clauses.spa: fue hecha pedazos por Ezequías, porque Israel le había quemado incienso
clauses.renderingsChanged: Subject «Israel» as in the English instead of «children/sons of Israel»; German archaic «zerstoßen»/«geräuchert» and Spanish «perfumes» modernised, with the pluperfect restored.

first.reason: The verses state two chief events of the object: Moses made it and those bitten who looked at it lived, and Hezekiah later broke it after Israel burned incense to it.
doubts: JHN 3:14 compares the lifting up of the serpent to the Son of man; this is a comparison, not an event, so it was left out.
2KI 18:4 does not name Hezekiah in the given verses; the summary supplies him.

declined.name: Ashbel
declined.reason: Every verse that names Ashbel only lists him among the sons of Benjamin or as head of a family, which is no more than the summary already says.

declined.name: Elkanah
declined.reason: The verses only list Elkanah in Levitical genealogies and give no deed or event beyond the family relations the summary already states.
